answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral and shared behavioral evidence: when k identities coordinate equivocation, aggregate penalties scale quadratically, O(k^2), rather than linearly. Once detected, controlling the swarm incurs an exponential multiplier in capital loss, making coordinated fraud economically prohibitive. Whether presented as an ember, relic, or mesa of independent agents, correlated proofs expose the common controller and erase any voting-power advantage.
